title: Michael Burry won't buy Nvidia stock 'at any price,' sees more trouble
excerpt: Michael Burry of "The Big Short" fame says he won't buy Nvidia stock even if it crashes, as he expects more trouble beyond the Jensen Huang scandal.
content_html:
Michael Burry says he won't buy Nvidia stock 'at any price' now — as he predicts 'real problems' beyond Jensen Huang

By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-16T15:45:22.764Z

Michael Burry says he won't buy Nvidia stock even if it falls further, as he's bracing for more bad news.

"My spidey sense tingles that something is still wrong," the investor of "The Big Short" fame wrote in a Substack post on Sunday.

Nvidia's founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, resigned on Thursday following reports that he had extramarital affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and one of his direct reports.

"I will not touch buying this stock at any price in the near term," Burry wrote. "I fear there are real problems with Nvidia that still will come to light."

Nvidia stock was flat at roughly $162 in early trading on Monday, around a third below the all-time high of $243 it touched on October 6, less than six weeks ago. The company's market capitalization has tumbled from around $5.8 trillion at its peak to below $4 trillion.

Burry — who pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing about his personal investments a year ago — said on Substack that he was concerned about Nvidia's purchase commitments, the future of the complex ecosystem it built, and its central role in the AI boom.

Burry also said he was watching for "competitors and customers taking advantage" of Nvidia's troubles by negotiating lower prices and later purchases of chips.

Those developments could shrink the company's profit margins and stop it from selling chips long before its customers have finished building the data centers to use them.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Elon Musk went further in an X post on Saturday, warning that many of Nvidia's deals were a "handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," and "at least some of those critical deals will be lost" without Huang at the helm.

Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract. Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 14, 2026

Burry is best known for predicting and profiting from the crash of the mid-2000s housing bubble, after his prescient bet was chronicled in the book and movie "The Big Short."

He wrote in a Friday post that he still owned put options on Nvidia stock that were scheduled to expire next February, and owned bearish puts on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF and the Nasdaq 100, both of which count Nvidia as a major constituent.

Burry has taken aim at Nvidia repeatedly over the past year, warning it's highly exposed to an AI slowdown as it has invested heavily in AI stocks, aggressively financed its customers' purchases of its chips, and essentially positioned itself as the lynchpin of the entire industry.
